question_record.context: There is an ongoing security incident involving suspicious activities on host `mb-adfs` where an account with name `gsmith` and account Sid `S-2-5-21-571436798-3864380397-1837441745-3206` executed a file `iy2orr1e.rrg.exe` using command line `3116__2024-07-02t09:48:23.9439954z__"iy2orr1e.rrg.exe" -windowstyle hidden -encodedcommand qwa6afwauwbjahiaaqbwahqacwbcaeuaeabwag8acgb0aeearabgafmavabvagsazqbuafmaaqbnag4aaqbuaemazqbyahqalgbwahmamqa=`. The incident includes hands-on-keyboard attacks via the Impacket toolkit and code injection activities, indicating possible attempts to move laterally across the network and execute malicious payloads.
question_record.question: Can you identify the AadUserId of the account that was associated with the process that injected potentially malicious code?
solution: A known public tool was observed under an unexpected filename, which might be an attempt to hide the usage of that tool for malicious purposes by an account with AadUserId `ec3ec68b-fdeb-4fe4-9a29-acd445e1ccc5`.

Suspicious execution of a command via Impacket toolkit was observed, using the process `powershell.exe`. This indicates a potential hands-on-keyboard attack where attackers might be attempting to move laterally across the network.

A process was injected with potentially malicious code by an account with AadUserId `a2d0f7c2-b0a0-43bd-bce0-27d8ae3be4d0`. This injected code indicates suspicious activity as the target process may behave abnormally, such as opening a listening port or connecting to a command and control server.

32.name: Attempt to hide use of dual-purpose tool
32.description:
A known public tool, which could also be used for malicious reasons, was observed under an unexpected filename.
This might be an attempt to hide the usage of that tool for malicious purposes.

16.name: Ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via Impacket toolkit
16.description:
Suspicious execution of a command via Impacket was observed on this device. This tool connects to other hosts to explore network shares and execute commands. Attackers might be attempting to move laterally across the network using this tool. This usage of Impacket has often been observed in hands-on-keyboard attacks, where ransomware and other payloads are installed on target devices.

Corresponding TA for this IOA: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/ff7e4fff-dde3-49be-9a06-7f63a490996d/analystreport

41.name: A process was injected with potentially malicious code
41.description:
A process has injected code into another process, indicating suspicious code being run in the target process memory. Injection is often used to hide malicious code execution within a trusted process. 
As a result, the target process may exhibit abnormal behaviors such as opening a listening port or connecting to a command and control server.
